title: How Banks Create Money
objective: After this level you can explain how bank lending creates most of the money in circulation.
summary: A new bank loan creates a matching deposit: new money. Most money today starts this way. Repaying destroys it, and profit, risk, rules and interest rates limit it.

cards.headline: When a bank lends you money, it doesn't hand you anyone's savings.
cards.body: It creates a brand-new deposit in your account. According to the Bank of England, that's where most of today's money comes from.

cards.headline: Money at the stroke of a pen
cards.body: Say you take out a mortgage to buy a house. The bank doesn't count out banknotes. It credits your account with a new deposit the size of the loan, and at that moment new money exists that didn't before. Some economists call this "fountain pen money", created at the stroke of a banker's pen when a loan is approved. The pen is optional these days.

cards.headline: Level 21, flipped
cards.body: Level 21 showed a bank standing between savers and borrowers. The Bank of England says the order usually runs the other way: rather than lending out deposits that savers placed with them, banks create deposits by lending. That's how Level 8's 97% came about. Most of the money people hold in banks started life as somebody's loan.

mascot.line: Easy to get backwards: banks don't lend out deposits first. The loan creates the deposit.

cards.fact: Paying off a loan makes money disappear.
cards.context: Repaying a bank loan destroys the deposit that lending created. And banks can't create money without limit: they must lend profitably and manage their risks, regulators set rules, and the central bank's interest rates act as the ultimate brake.

cards.headline: Money creation: decoded
learned: A new loan creates a matching new deposit
Most money today starts as bank lending
Repaying a loan destroys that money
Profit, risk, rules and rates limit it

questions.prompt: A bank approves your loan. Where does the money in your account come from?

options.label: It's moved over from other customers' savings
options.rationale: That's the textbook picture; in fact, lending creates a new deposit.

options.label: The bank creates a new deposit for you
The central bank prints fresh banknotes
options.rationale: No banknotes are involved: the bank credits your account.

options.label: It's taken from the bank's gold reserves
options.rationale: No gold moves: the loan creates a new deposit.

questions.explanation: Making a loan credits the borrower's account with a matching new deposit, which is new money.

questions.prompt: Why can't a bank create unlimited money by lending?

options.label: Every loan must be matched by gold in its vault
options.rationale: The gold link is long gone. Profit, risk, rules and rates limit lending.

options.label: It must lend profitably, follow rules and face interest rates
The law caps each bank at a fixed number of customers
options.rationale: No such cap: the limits are profit, risk, regulation and rates.

options.label: Borrowers must deposit cash before any loan
options.rationale: Lending creates the deposit; no cash has to come first.

questions.explanation: Banks must lend profitably and manage risk, regulators constrain them, and central bank interest rates are the ultimate limit.

questions.prompt: Level 8 said 97% of UK money is bank deposits. Where did most of those deposits come from?

options.label: Banknotes that people paid into banks
options.rationale: Deposits mostly start as loans, not paid-in cash.

options.label: Gold that banks bought and stored
options.rationale: Gold plays no part: lending creates the deposits.

options.label: The central bank's printing presses
options.rationale: Presses make notes, which are only about 3% of UK money.

questions.explanation: Most money is created by commercial banks lending: each loan creates a matching deposit.
